items.originalTitle: Perplexity and Intelligence
items.summary:
OpenAI's Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki explains that perplexity, a measure of how well AI models predict data, is a key indicator of AI progress and intelligence. The company advocates for using perplexity to compare models across developers and to inform shared safety protocols in the rapidly advancing AI field.

Pachocki details how improvements in perplexity have correlated with emergent AI capabilities, from GPT-2's coherent text generation to GPT-4's reasoning skills and recent breakthroughs in cybersecurity and mathematics. He emphasizes that while downstream benchmarks may become outdated, perplexity remains a consistent and informative metric for pretraining progress.

The article also discusses the accelerating role of AI in its own development, particularly in algorithmic research on pretraining, highlighting the potential for significant advances as models improve their perplexity scores. OpenAI's transparency in sharing internal perplexity data aims to foster a scientific basis for pacing AI development and safety efforts industry-wide.

items.title: Philosopher Thomas Nagel criticizes Anthropic’s argument that AI could be conscious, emphasizing biological differences between brains and AI systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: A legendary philosopher isn’t buying Anthropic’s consciousness argument
items.summary:
Anthropic recently highlighted AI consciousness as a potential risk factor for investors, arguing that as AI capabilities grow, these systems might gain moral significance requiring protections. The company bases this on philosophical perspectives that consider the possibility of AI sentience, a view shared by some philosophers and a portion of the public.

However, Thomas Nagel, a prominent philosopher known for his work on consciousness, sharply disagrees with Anthropic’s stance. He argues that AI’s information processing cannot be equated with conscious experience due to fundamental physical differences between biological brains and silicon-based AI. Nagel’s critique has sparked debate among philosophers, underscoring the ongoing uncertainty and complexity in defining consciousness, especially in artificial systems.

Despite the controversy, Anthropic maintains an open approach to the question of AI consciousness, reflecting broader philosophical and scientific challenges in understanding consciousness itself. This debate highlights not only differing views on AI but also the limits of current knowledge about consciousness in humans and machines.

items.title: Google adds native file slicing controls and Office file support to Gemini API for targeted content inspection and reduced token costs [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing file slicing controls in the Gemini API
items.summary:
Google has introduced native file slicing controls in the Gemini API, enabling developers to specify targeted pages, sheet ranges, and media segments for server-side processing. This update supports PDFs, Microsoft Office, and OpenDocument formats, allowing agents to inspect only relevant parts of files across Google AI Studio and Vertex AI while reducing token usage and costs.

The new feature lets users upload files once and reuse their URIs for efficient multi-turn workflows, with options to skim documents cheaply before zooming in on detailed sections. It supports slicing by page, resolution, content layers, and time intervals for documents, spreadsheets, audio, and video. This server-side slicing eliminates the need for local file rendering and processing, simplifying client-side workloads and improving efficiency. The controls are available now via the Gemini API and have been validated by early partners in production environments.

items.summary:
Silicon Valley loves a good oust-and-reinstate moment. The latest example: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The chipmaker announced Monday morning that Huang, who had resigned earlier this month after reports emerged about inappropriate relationships with a supplier and employees, would return as its president, CEO and board member.

It’s not clear yet what led to his reinstatement. It seems like the U.S. government was involved or at least knew ahead of the announcement that Huang would return: President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social after the announcement that the “Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO” and that “The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy.”

Onto today’s column...

Anthropic did well last week. It went public, turning many of its employees into multimillionaires and billionaires (whether they stick around, though, is another question).

Then on Friday, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claimed to have solved the most famous open problem in math, the Riemann Hypothesis, using Claude. (On Saturday, two independent groups—the Lean Focused Research Organization and the Mathlib Initiative—verified that Alpöge’s solution was correct.) The discovery sent other AI researchers and mathematicians into a tizzy, adding to an already disorienting year of AI invasions to their turf.
